about.title: Personal Injury Help in Healdsburg, California
about.longDescription: Healdsburg's small-town streets carry a lot of traffic for a town of 11,742 people, especially where Healdsburg Avenue, Dry Creek Road, and US-101 funnel commuters, wine-country visitors, and delivery trucks through the same stretches. In the most recent full year on record, the city logged 18 injury collisions and 21 people hurt, with no traffic deaths reported. Collisions have tended to bunch up on Saturday afternoons between 4 and 6 p.m., a pattern consistent with weekend errands, tasting-room traffic, and US-101 southbound backups. If you were hurt in any of these situations, we can help. We handle personal injury claims throughout Sonoma County, and we work on contingency, meaning there's no cost to you unless your case results in a recovery. Reaching out costs nothing, and our team can look at what happened and explain your options under California law.

whyChoose.title: Why Talk to an Attorney Soon

items.title: The Clock Is Running
items.desc: California generally gives you two years from the date of injury to file a claim, but if a government entity (like a city road crew) may be involved, that window can shrink to as little as six months. Waiting too long can cost you the right to recover anything.

items.title: Partial Fault Doesn't Shut You Out
items.desc: Under California's pure comparative fault rule, even if you were partly responsible for what happened, you can still recover damages — reduced by your share of fault, not eliminated by it.

items.title: No Ceiling on Pain-and-Suffering Damages
items.desc: In ordinary injury cases, California places no cap on non-economic damages like pain, suffering, and loss of enjoyment of life, so these losses can be fully considered.

items.title: No Fee Unless You Recover
items.desc: We work on contingency. That means you pay nothing upfront, and there's no attorney fee unless your case results in a settlement or award.

items.question: How long do I have to file a personal injury claim in Healdsburg?
items.answer: California generally allows two years from the date of the injury to file a claim. If your accident involved a government entity, such as a road or public agency, that deadline can be as short as six months, so it's worth checking your specific situation sooner rather than later.

items.question: What if I was partly at fault for the accident?
items.answer: California follows pure comparative fault, which means you can still recover compensation even if you share some blame. Your recovery is simply reduced by your percentage of fault, not wiped out entirely.

items.question: Where do crashes tend to cluster in Healdsburg?
items.answer: Public collision records show higher volumes along Healdsburg Avenue, Dry Creek Road, and US-101, including the southbound direction, with reported activity often peaking on Saturdays between 4 and 6 p.m. These are simply the corridors with the most recorded collisions, not a judgment about any particular road.

items.question: Do you charge me anything?
items.answer: No. We provide a free case review for injured people in Sonoma County. We never charge you for the initial consultation.

items.question: Will I have to pay attorney fees upfront?
items.answer: We work on contingency, meaning we only get paid if your case results in a settlement or award. There's no upfront cost to you for legal representation.
